target: Smith restricted maximum-length question: positive factorizations of one boundary twist on a fixed-genus one-boundary surface with pairwise geometric intersections at most one.
hypotheses: Compact connected oriented genus-g surface with one boundary component; g >= 1 fixed.
Orientation-preserving mapping classes fix the boundary pointwise.
All factors are positive twists about non-null-homotopic simple closed curves; disk-bounding twists excluded.
Pairwise geometric intersection at most one; repeated isotopy classes allowed.
Boundary-parallel factors permitted in the broader convention; they occur only as the singleton factorization.
accepted_conclusions: Finitely many admissible ordered factorizations modulo simultaneous boundary-fixing orientation-preserving conjugation.
The length maximum M(g) exists and 4g(2g+1) <= M(g) < infinity.

Every admissible factorization except the peripheral singleton uses only nonseparating curves, by the parity condition and credited Smith invariant-curve theorem with an explicit Lefschetz construction.
Credited low-genus maxima M(1)=12 and M(2)=40.
remaining_gap: Determine M(g) for g >= 3, give an explicit genus-dependent upper-bound formula and prove any asserted extremizer classification. No Hurwitz, positive-Artin, T-move or A5/D6 classification is supplied.
